content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP® Certification in Savannah

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your PMI Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-leadership experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Verify your education and documented hours directing projects. Granite PM Academy can review your background to ensure you meet the baseline before enrolling in the bootcamp.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP® bootcamp. You'll attend instructor-led sessions covering the PMBOK® Guide framework, risk management, stakeholder engagement, and exam strategy. All sessions are remote and scheduled to fit working professionals' calendars. Upon completion, you receive the required certificate of training hours.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Register with PMI and submit your official application, including your education credentials and project experience documentation. Pay the PMI examination fee through their portal. PMI will review and approve your application, typically within two weeks. Once approved, you'll receive authorization to schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-prep resources, including practice questions, mock exams, and study guides aligned to the PMP® blueprint. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center in Savannah or online proctored. The four-hour, 180-question exam tests your mastery of project management domains and readiness for your local job market.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you hold the PMP® credential for three years. Earn 60 professional development units (PDUs) during each three-year cycle through training, conferences, volunteer work, or on-the-job practice. Renew before expiration to keep your credential active and remain competitive in Savannah's growing project-management roles.
